samples.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one small coloured medallion: a solid central disk wrapped in four concentric rings of equal thickness. Every ring is split down its vertical middle, so it has a left half of one colour and a right half of a different colour. Every coloured part of the medallion is red, green, blue, purple or orange. The colour of the central disk is the colour carried at the start. Each ring is one swap rule between its own two half colours: when the colour carried at that moment is one of that ring's two half colours it becomes the ring's other half colour, and otherwise that ring does nothing at all. The rings act one after another, beginning with the innermost ring, which touches the central disk, and working outwards to the outermost ring, so the order matters. The medallion may sit anywhere on the canvas, and every grey mark outside it is inert decoration that changes nothing. Which colour is carried after the outermost ring has acted? Answer with one of red, green, blue, purple or orange.
